candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Rewrite quantities into equivalent subtraction-ready forms, including finding a common denominator, converting to equivalent fractions, simplifying a fraction part before subtraction, or rewriting a whole number with a fractional part.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S01 and B.S01 are essentially identical. C.S01 matches the common-denominator and whole-number-with-fractional-part portions of that concept; C separates normalization of improper mixed-number parts into a distinct skill, whereas A and B include that inside their broader rewrite skill.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Rewrite a mixed number with a nonstandard or improper fractional part into an equivalent standard mixed number before subtraction.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: Only expert C isolates normalization of mixed numbers as its own skill. In A and B, this operation is embedded within their broader rewrite skills (A.S01 and B.S01), but because every skill_id must appear exactly once, those broader skills are aligned to the larger rewrite concept rather than duplicated here.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Perform subtraction once quantities are in compatible form, including subtracting like fractions and subtracting whole and fractional parts of mixed numbers when no regrouping is required.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S02, B.S02, and C.S03 all describe the core subtraction step after alignment. C.S03 is slightly broader because it may include expressing the direct result, but its central cognitive operation matches A and B.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Regroup by taking 1 from the whole-number part and converting it into fractional units so subtraction can continue when the fractional part of the minuend is too small.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S03 and B.S03 are direct matches. Expert C does not separate borrowing from simplification; instead, borrowing is folded into C.S04 together with result simplification, so no standalone C skill maps uniquely to this concept.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Reduce the subtraction result to lowest terms and express it appropriately as a fraction, mixed number, integer, or zero form.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S04 and B.S04 are direct matches. C.S04 includes this same simplification/final-expression concept but combines it with borrowing/regrouping, making C's skill broader than A and B.

alignment_summary: The three codebooks share strong agreement on the major workflow: rewrite into subtraction-ready form, subtract aligned parts, borrow/regroup when needed, and simplify/express the result. Experts A and B are nearly identical. Expert C uses a different granularity: it splits normalization of improper mixed numbers into its own skill and combines borrowing with simplification into one broader skill. The alignment preserves all skill_ids exactly once while noting these granularity differences.
